blocks.content: These are the fields sent in the JSON body to the POST /v1/messages endpoint. Three are required; the rest modify behavior or enable additional features.

rows: The model identifier, e.g. claude-sonnet-4-6. Determines cost per token, speed, and reasoning capability.
The full conversation up to this point. Each object has role (user or assistant) and content. The API is stateless: you have to resend the entire history on every call.
Maximum number of tokens to generate. The model can stop earlier if it finishes naturally. If the response hits this limit exactly, stop_reason will be max_tokens.
Context, role, and rule instructions that apply from the first turn. Sent as a separate field, not inside messages.
Controls randomness. Low values = predictable, focused responses. High values = more variation. As of Opus 4.7 (including Opus 4.8): sending a non-default value returns a 400 error.
Nucleus sampling: only considers the set of tokens whose cumulative probability reaches this threshold. As of Opus 4.7 (including Opus 4.8): sending a non-default value returns a 400 error.
Limits sampling to the k most probable tokens at each step. Older technique, rarely needed. As of Opus 4.7 (including Opus 4.8): sending a non-default value returns a 400 error.
Text sequences that, when they appear, immediately stop generation. Useful for cutting the response off at an exact, predictable point.
If true, the response arrives incrementally via server-sent events instead of waiting for the full message.
Additional information, such as your own user_id to track usage per end user without exposing identifiable data to Anthropic.
Defines external functions Claude can invoke: name, description, and an input_schema in JSON Schema. Claude decides when and how to use them.
Controls whether Claude should use a tool: auto (decides on its own), any (must use one), tool (forces a specific one), or none.
Enables extended thinking, where the model exposes its reasoning process before responding. Requires a budget_tokens.
Connects remote MCP servers so Claude can use external tools directly from the API.
Configures the output format. output_config.format with type: json_schema guarantees valid JSON with the exact structure specified.

blocks.title: temperature, top_p, and top_k are mutually exclusive
blocks.content: Using more than one at a time produces unpredictable results. For most use cases, adjusting only temperature is enough.

blocks.title: Deprecated as of Opus 4.7: use effort or prompting instead
blocks.content: As of Opus 4.7 (and in Opus 4.8), sending `temperature`, `top_p`, or `top_k` with a value other than the default returns a **400 error**. Anthropic's official recommendation is to omit these three parameters entirely and control model behavior with prompting or with the `output_config.effort` parameter (`low`/`medium`/`high`/`xhigh`/`max`). Sonnet and Haiku aren't affected by this restriction.

subsections.title: What stop_reason is and why it matters

blocks.content: stop_reason indicates why the model stopped generating. It's the most important control signal for building robust agent logic: don't just read the generated text — always check stop_reason to know what the code should do next.

rows: The model finished its response naturally.
The max_tokens limit was reached. The response may be incomplete.
Consider continuing generation or raising the limit depending on the case.
The model generated one of the sequences defined in stop_sequences.
Extract the content up to the sequence and process it.
Claude requested to execute a tool and is waiting for the result.
Execute the tools from the content block and return the results as tool_result.
Pause related to server-side tools (web search, etc.).
Just forward the assistant's response as-is so it can continue.
Claude declined to generate a response for safety reasons.
The response may contain partial content. Don't retry with the same input.
The model's context window limit was reached.
Reduce the message history or use context compaction.

blocks.title: refusal comes with stop_details for more context
blocks.content: When stop_reason is "refusal", the response includes a stop_details field with type ("refusal"), category, and explanation. category and explanation can come back as null if the refusal doesn't map to any named policy category — don't assume they're always populated. It's better to branch on stop_reason or stop_details.type, not on category.

blocks.code:
response = client.messages.create(
    model="claude-sonnet-4-6",
    max_tokens=1024,
    messages=messages,
)

match response.stop_reason:
    case "end_turn":
        return response.content[0].text
    case "max_tokens":
        # the response may be truncated
        continue_generation(response)
    case "tool_use":
        # extract the tool_use blocks and execute them
        blocks = [b for b in response.content if b.type == "tool_use"]
        execute_tools(blocks)
    case "refusal":
        raise ValueError("Claude declined to respond")
    case "model_context_window_exceeded":
        messages = compact_history(messages)
        retry()

blocks.content: The API follows a predictable error format. The response body always includes type and message inside an error object.

rows: Problem with the format or content of the request: a misspelled parameter, a nonexistent model, or prefill on a model that no longer supports it.
There's a problem with the API key: missing, malformed, or invalid.
The API key doesn't have permission to use the requested resource.
The request exceeds the maximum allowed size (32 MB on standard endpoints).
A rate limit was exceeded: requests per minute, input tokens per minute, or output tokens per minute. The response includes a retry-after header.
Unexpected internal error in Anthropic's systems.
The API is temporarily overloaded due to high traffic. Not an account limit: retry with exponential backoff.

blocks.title: Retry strategy
blocks.content: For 429 and 529, use exponential backoff starting at 1-5 seconds. For 400, 401, 403, and 404, retrying doesn't help: you need to fix the request before trying again.

With stream: true, the response arrives as a sequence of events via Server-Sent Events instead of a single JSON block at the end. Useful when you want to show the response to the user as it's generated.

rows: Arrives first, with an empty Message object that marks the start of the response.
Marks the start of a new content block (text, tool_use, etc.).
Many of these arrive in sequence, each with an incremental fragment of text or JSON.
Includes message-level changes, such as the final stop_reason and the usage count.
Signals that the response has fully ended.

blocks.code:
with client.messages.stream(
    model="claude-sonnet-4-6",
    max_tokens=1024,
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Write a short poem"}],
) as stream:
    for text in stream.text_stream:
        print(text, end="", flush=True)

# To access stop_reason and usage after the stream:
final_response = stream.get_final_message()
print(final_response.stop_reason)
print(final_response.usage)
